event.canonical_title: Teen Charged with Murder for Livestreaming San Diego Mosque Attack
event.summary: A 17-year-old girl from North Carolina has been charged with murder for her involvement in the San Diego mosque shooting that occurred on May 18. Prosecutors allege that she recorded the attack and shared a manifesto from the shooters. She will be charged as an adult.

event_overview.title: About Charlie Kirk Murder Case
event_overview.subject: Charlie Kirk Murder Case
event_overview.summary: The Charlie Kirk murder case is a Utah state criminal prosecution arising from the fatal shooting of conservative activist and Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk during an outdoor event at Utah Valley University in Orem on September 10, 2025. Tyler James Robinson is the defendant; the allegations remain to be resolved through the criminal-court process, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

facts.label: Incident
facts.value: The charging document alleges that Kirk was killed in Utah County on September 10, 2025, during an appearance at Utah Valley University in Orem, Utah.

facts.label: Court and parties
facts.value: The matter is State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson in Utah's Fourth Judicial District Court, Utah County; the Utah County Attorney's Office filed the criminal information on September 16, 2025.

facts.label: Charges
facts.value: Robinson was charged with aggravated murder, felony discharge of a firearm causing serious bodily injury, two counts of obstruction of justice, two counts of witness tampering, and a violent-offense-in-the-presence-of-a-child charge.

facts.label: Capital-case scope
facts.value: The aggravated-murder count was filed as a capital felony, alleging that the defendant knowingly created a great risk of death to someone other than Kirk and himself; prosecutors have sought a death sentence, which would require separate capital-sentencing proceedings if there were a qualifying conviction.

facts.label: Procedural posture as of September 2, 20
facts.value: Following a preliminary hearing, the court found sufficient evidence for the case to proceed to trial on the charges, including aggravated murder; a finding at that stage is not a determination of guilt.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows major developments in the Charlie Kirk prosecution rather than every filing, hearing, or evidentiary claim; the listed September 1 San Diego mosque-attack item concerns a separate case and is not part of this prosecution.
